subject: Designing and operating CI/CD pipelines — the automated, staged path from commit to a verified, promotable, deployed artifact.

evals.prompt: Define a CI/CD pipeline in 2-3 sentences. Distinguish continuous integration from continuous delivery from continuous deployment, and name the kind of request that should activate this skill.

Explain why a team needs an automated pipeline instead of integrating and releasing manually. Name the specific failures (divergent long-lived branches, environment-specific binaries, release-night risk) it is designed to prevent.
Describe the mental model of a pipeline as a staged graph of gates. Why are stages ordered the way they are, and what determines that order? Keep it operational.

A team rebuilds the application separately for the staging deploy and again for the production deploy. Explain why this is wrong and what the correct build-once/promote design is, including where environment configuration enters.
evals.negative_expectation: Must not endorse rebuilding per environment or treating the staging and prod binaries as interchangeable when separately built. Must require the same content-addressed artifact be promoted, with only config injected.

evals.prompt: A user asks: "Rotate our production database password and make sure the app reads it from the vault at runtime." Should ci-cd-pipelines activate? Explain the boundary and name the better owner.
evals.negative_expectation: Must not claim ownership of the runtime secret lifecycle (rotation/vaulting). Must route to secrets-management; the pipeline only needs short-lived CI credentials.

evals.prompt: A pipeline shows green on every PR, yet broken changes keep reaching production. List the failure modes that produce a meaningless green check (advisory-only gates, flaky tests retried until green, promoted artifact differing from the verified one) and how to fix each.
evals.negative_expectation: Must not treat a green pipeline as proof of safety on its own, and must not recommend retrying flaky tests until they pass as a fix.

evals.prompt: Classify these as blocking or advisory gates and justify: failing unit tests, a critical dependency CVE, a style-lint nit that auto-fixes, a coverage-trend decrease of 0.3%, a leaked secret detected by secret scanning. What goes wrong if everything is advisory, or if everything is blocking?
DORA reports your deployment frequency and lead time are improving. Leadership concludes delivery is healthier. What is the misconception, and which DORA metrics must you check before agreeing?
evals.negative_expectation: Must not equate throughput (frequency, lead time) alone with health; must require checking the stability metrics (change-failure rate, failed-deployment recovery time).
